02 / 08 Automotive

GetMOTO

Motorbike repair and rental · Luton, United Kingdom

A scooter that comes apart, part by part, as you scroll.

A one-page website for a motorcycle and scooter workshop in Luton: repairs, key programming, MOT preparation and rentals. The opening is a 150-frame sequence in which the scooter comes apart as you scroll; rentals and bookings open WhatsApp with the request already filled in.

  • 150-frame sequence
  • GSAP ScrollTrigger
  • Rentals via WhatsApp

03 / 08 Bars

Chez TonTon

Bar and bottle shop · Pontchâteau, France

From the cold of the fridge to the warmth of the counter.

A bar and bottle shop in Pontchâteau: beers and wines to enjoy on site or take away. The opening starts inside the fridge; a bottle lifts out of the shot, the cold light gives way to a cream beer poster, and the poster hands the scene over to the real bar.

La Cabane à Mousse

Beer cellar, bar and tap hire · Herbignac, France

A toast between two glasses opens the page.

A beer cellar, bar and tap-hire business in Herbignac. On desktop the page is the approved design board rebuilt in HTML: the same toast and the same three chapters on torn paper, with real text over the imagery, sharp and readable by search engines.

Rumi Cafe

Turkish-Irish café · Dublin, Ireland

The steam from a coffee writes Rumi’s signature.

A family-run café on Francis Street, Dublin 8: speciality coffee, Turkish treats and a teal storefront everyone recognises. A multi-page website with an 18-item menu with search and filters, story, gallery, club and gift cards; orders carry on to the café’s ordering site.

07 / 08 Ice cream

isola

Ice cream shop · Mosede Havn, Denmark

Four flavours, four universes, one scene.

An ice cream shop by the harbour in Mosede. The page opens on a stable composition, the headline on the left and a scoop suspended over a waffle cone, and lets the flavour change around it: pistachio, salted caramel, mango and raspberry, by scroll or with the selector.

  • 2.5D scene from 14 cut-outs
  • Flavour selector
  • Copy in Danish

08 / 08 Barbershop

Bayro Cut

Barbershop · Greve, Denmark

The clipper leaves the barber’s hand and finishes the cut.

A barbershop inside WAVES in Greve: men’s cuts, fades and beards, booked by phone. The opening is a scroll-driven scene in which the clipper leaves the barber’s hand, opens into body, blade and guide comb, runs along the fade, and the portrait lands in the gallery.

  • Scroll-driven 2.5D scene
  • Parts registered with OpenCV

About · behind the vision

Technology starts with people.

I’m Josean Araújo. My path connects software implementation, solution presentation and web development. In Dublin, with Microsoft, I brought business challenges and technology together. In Paris, at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, I led presentation and training for the HPE Flex Offers programme across France.

Today I bring that experience to design, code and artificial intelligence: I create digital experiences and connect tools into workflows.

I like to think about the whole experience: the first impression, what happens in each interaction and how technology becomes useful to the person on the other side.

Experience

  1. 2022 — 2023 Paris, France

    Hewlett Packard Enterprise

    Head of Presentation and Training · HPE Flex Offers programme

    • Led the HPE Flex Offers presentation and training programme across France.
    • Delivered 10 to 15 workshops and strategic presentations to more than 100 enterprise clients and partners.
    • Translated infrastructure modernisation into clear business value for each audience, alongside the sales, marketing and engineering teams.
    • Received the company’s internal award for two consecutive months for results above expectations.

  2. 2020 — 2021 Dublin, Ireland

    Microsoft / Infosys

    Technical Solutions Consultant · Business Technology Advisor

    • Presented Microsoft solutions with a customer-focused, business-oriented approach.
    • Qualified client needs and translated business challenges into technology recommendations.
    • Connected business priorities, technical teams and delivery in a multicultural environment.
